'''''Hakea decurrens''''', commonly known as  '''bushy needlewood''',<ref name="RBGV"/> is a [[species]]  of shrub or small tree in the family [[Proteaceae]].

==Description==
''Hakea decurrens'' is a semi-prostrate to erect scrambling bush or  small tree {{convert|0.4-5|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} tall.  Smaller branches have short densely matted silky hairs, occasionally some quickly becoming smooth. Leaves are needle-shaped, widely spreading horizontally, are {{convert|1.5-8|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|0.7-1.6|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide. The smooth leaves are grooved on the underside ending with a sharp point {{convert|1-3.5|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long. The  [[inflorescence]] consists in 1–6 white or pink flowers on a short white or rusty slightly hairy or densely matted hairy short stalk. The hairs extending onto a {{convert|1.2-4.8|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long [[pedicel (botany)|pedicel]]. The smooth [[perianth]] is {{convert|4.2-7.2|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long. The [[Style (botany)|style]] is {{convert|8.5-12.2|mm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} long. A profusion of flowers appear in leaf axils from May to September. The grey woody fruit are broadly egg-shaped, {{convert|1.8–3.5|cm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and  {{convert|1–3|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide, covered in distinct warts ending in a prominent beak with two small horns.<ref name="RBGV">{{cite web |title=''Hakea decurrens'' |url=https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/9e041a12-c521-4e23-8d3a-8318be8c7bf8 |website=VicFlora-Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria |access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref><ref name="DUI">{{cite book |last1=Holliday |first1=Ivan |title=Hakeas a Field and Garden Guide |date=2005 |publisher=Reed New Holland |isbn=1-877069-14-0}}</ref><ref name="W&F">{{cite book |last1=Wrigley |first1=John W. |last2=Fagg |first2=Murray |title=Banksias, Waratahs & Grevilleas & all other plants in the Australian Proteaceae Family |date=1989 |publisher=Collins Australia |isbn=0-7322-0020-2}}</ref><ref name="SAF">{{cite web |title=''Hakea decurrens'' |url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/efsa/lucid/Hakea/key/Australian%20Hakea%20species/Media/Html/Hakea_decurrens_ssp._decurrens.htm |website=Flora of South Australia |publisher=South Australian Government |access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref><ref name="FOAB"/>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Hakea decurrens'' was first formally described in 1830 by [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] in ''[[Supplementum primum prodromi florae Novae Hollandiae]]''.<ref name="APNI">{{cite web |title=''Hakea decurrens'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/rest/instance/apni/477076 |publisher=Australian Plant Name Index |access-date=26 July 2025}}</ref>
The [[specific epithet]] (''decurrens'') is a [[Latin]] word, meaning "decurrent" or "prolonged below the point of insertion", referring to the insertion of the leaf on the stem.<ref name="SAF"/>

In 1996, [[William Robert Barker (botanist)|William Robert Barker]] described three subspecies of ''Hakea decurrens'' in the ''[[Journal of the Adelaide Botanic Gardens]]'' and the names are accepted by the [[Australian Plant Census]].<ref name="Barker">{{cite journal |last1=Barker |first1=William R. |title=Novelties and taxonomic notes relating to ''Hakea'' (Proteaceae), mainly of eastern Australia. |journal=Journal of the Adelaide Botanic Gardens |date=1996 |volume=17 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/23873904 |access-date=22 June 2022}}</ref>

* ''Hakea decurrens'' subsp. ''decurrens''<ref name="APC1">{{cite web |title=''Hakea decurrens'' subsp. ''decurrens'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/164854 |website=Australian Plant Census |access-date=22 June 2022}}</ref> on younger branches has flattened hairs, quickly becoming smooth and the fruit {{convert|1-1.8|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide;<ref name="SAF"/><ref name="FOAB">{{cite book |editor-last1=Wilson |editor-first1=Annette |editor-last2=Barker |editor-first2=Robyn M. |editor-last3=Haegi |editor-first3=Laurence A. |editor-last4=Barker |editor-first4=William R. |title=Flora of Australia |volume=17B |date=1999 |publisher=ABRS-Department of Environment & Heritage |location=Canberra/Melbourne |isbn=0-643-06454-0 |url=http://www.environment.gov.au/system/files/pages/6d8c5c3b-8545-437e-b9b3-944ac95ee07a/files/flora-australia-17b-proteaceae-3-hakea-dryandra.pdf}}</ref>
* ''Hakea decurrens'' subsp. ''platytaenia''<ref name="APC2">{{cite web |title=''Hakea decurrens'' subsp. ''platytaenia''|url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/163558 |website=Australian Plant Census |access-date=22 June 2022}}</ref> has persistent raised hairs and fruit {{convert|2.6-3.5|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide;<ref name="SAF"/><ref name="FOAB"/>
* ''Hakea decurrens'' subsp. ''physocarpa''<ref name="APC3">{{cite web |title=''Hakea decurrens'' subsp. ''physocarpa'' |url=https://biodiversity.org.au/nsl/services/apc-format/display/154116 |website=Australian Plant Census |access-date=22 June 2022}}</ref> has flattened hairs, quickly lost.  Fruit {{convert|1.3-2.5|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} wide.<ref name="SAF"/><ref name="FOAB"/>

==Distribution and habitat==
The species is native and widespread in [[New South Wales]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] and [[Tasmania]] in [[Australia]]. Additionally, it is naturalised in [[South Australia]] and [[Portugal]].

The distribution of the three subspecies is as follows:
* ''H. decurrens'' subsp. ''decurrens'', occurs on the western slopes and plains of the [[Great Dividing Range]] of New South Wales;<ref name="SAF"/><ref name="FOAB"/> 
* ''H. decurrens'' subsp. ''platytaenia'', occurs in exposed coastal heaths in southeastern New South Wales, eastern Victoria and the [[Bass Strait Islands]].<ref name="SAF"/><ref name="FOAB"/>
* ''H. decurrens'' subsp. ''physocarpa'', occurs in New South Wales, Victoria and the Bass Strait Islands.  In Tasmania it is thought to be native to the north and naturalised in the south. It is also naturalised in the [[Mount Lofty Ranges]] in South Australia and Portugal.<ref name="SAF"/><ref name="FOAB"/>
